title: A Versatile Method of Patterning Proteins and Cells
protocol: Draw the layout of the microchannel using a computer-aided design (CAD) drawing tool.
Print the layout on a blank mask plate using laser mask writer.
Rinse a 4 inch silicon wafer with acetone followed by isopropanol and dry with a nitrogen air gun to ensure that no solvent is left on the wafer.
Dehydrate the wafer by baking it on a hot plate at 200 °C for 5 min.
Allow the wafer to cool to room temperature, and then align the wafer on the chuck of a spin coater.
Dispense 4 mL (1 mL/inch diameter of the wafer) of negative photoresist onto the center of the wafer.
Spin coat the wafer with a two-step spin cycle using a spinner.
Apply a spread cycle of 500 rpm with an acceleration of 100 rpm/s for 10 s.
Apply a spin cycle of 2,000 rpm with an acceleration of 300 rpm/s2 for 30 s to obtain a 50 µm coating of photoresist on a wafer.
Soft bake the wafer in two steps on a hot plate according to the manufacturer's directions.
Pre-bake the wafer at 65 °C for 6 min and then immediately ramp up the hot plate temperature to post-bake the wafer at 95 °C for 20 min.
Allow the wafer to cool to room temperature and then load the wafer onto the lithography stage.

Align the mask on the wafer using a mask aligner and expose the wafer to UV light at an intensity of 1.5 mW/cm2 for 146 s to apply the total UV dose of 220 mJ/cm2 required for a 50 µm thick layer of photoresist.
Apply post exposure bake to the wafer in two steps on a hot plate.
Pre-bake the wafer at 65 °C for 1 min and immediately ramp up the hot plate temperature to post-bake it at 95 °C for 5 min.
Submerge the wafer in SU-8 developer and gently shake until features become clear on the wafer.
Develop the wafer for ~6 min for a 50 µm thick photoresist.
Rinse off excess developer with isopropanol and ethanol, then dry the wafer with a nitrogen air gun.
Hard bake the silicon wafer on a hot plate at 150 °C for 15 min.
Place the wafer in a desiccator with 25 µL of tridecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetrahydrooctyl-1-trichlorosilane.
Apply the vacuum for 5 min.
Expose the wafer to silane vapors for 30 min without releasing the vacuum.
Transfer the wafer into a suitably sized Petri dish.
Draw the layout of the microchannel using a CAD drawing tool.
Print the design on white paper.
Clean a glass slide with isopropanol and dry it with an air gun.
Attach adhesive tape onto the cleaned glass slide carefully to avoid trapping air bubbles.
Tape the sides of the glass slide onto the paper with the design, with the tape side up.
Cut the tape on the glass slide using the paper design as a reference.
Peel off tape from unwanted areas of the glass slide.
Rinse the glass slide with isopropanol and then dry it with an air gun.
Bake the glass slide in an oven at 65 °C for 30 min.
Gently roll over the tape with a rubber roller to remove air bubbles.
Allow the slide to cool to room temperature.
Mix PDMS elastomer and its curing agent in a ratio of 10:1 (w:w).
Stir the mixture vigorously.
Degas the mixture by placing it into a vacuum chamber until no air bubbles appear.
Pour the mixture onto a silanized silicon mold or adhesive tape mold in a petri dish to obtain a ~2 mm thick layer of PDMS.
Degas until all air bubbles disappear.
Cure the PDMS in an oven at 65 °C for 2 h.
Cut the PDMS layer at least 5 mm away from the features using a scalpel.
Peel the cured PDMS off the mold using tweezers.
Punch a single inlet hole with a 1 mm biopsy punch anywhere on the microchannel, preferably at the end of a network of microchannels.
Clean the PDMS cast with adhesive tape to remove dust particles adsorbed onto the device.
Rinse the PDMS microchannel device with a solution of 70% ethanol followed by sterile deionized (DI) water.
Expose the PDMS device to UV for 30 min.
Keep the sterile PDMS device in a sterile petri dish until use.
Place the sterile PDMS cast using tweezers onto a sterile glass coverslip or petri dish.
Apply gentle pressure using the tip of the tweezers.
Place a droplet (20 - 40 µL) of the substrate solution on the inlet completely covering the inlet hole.
Place a 20 µL droplet of PDL in sodium tetraborate buffer on the inlet of the microchannels.
Put the petri dish in a vacuum of ~254 mmHgA for 10 min.
Observe air coming out of the channel in the form of bubbles.
Release the vacuum and observe the substrate solution flowing into the microchannel.
Incubate the dish at 37 °C for 1 h to allow substrate adherence.
Carefully peel off the PDMS stamp using sterile tweezers.
Wash the pattern on glass coverslip thrice with DI water.
Add a 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) solution to cover the dish or the glass coverslip and incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Aspirate off the 1% BSA solution.
Prepare the cell suspension in serum-free culture medium.
Add the cell suspension to the patterned Petri dish completely submerging the patterned region.
Incubate the petri dish at 37 °C for 15 min to allow cells to attach to the patterned substrate.
Aspirate excess cell suspension from the Petri dish.
Wash patterned cells three times with phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Add appropriate culture medium to the patterned cell cultures.
Incubate patterned cells at 37 °C in a CO2 incubator.
Sterilize the microfluidic device by rinsing with 70% ethanol.
Rinse the sterilized device with DI water.
Soak the device overnight in a solution of 1% BSA.
Dry the device at room temperature.
Attach the dried device to the bottom of the tissue culture-treated Petri dish.
Prepare cell suspension in serum-free culture media.
Place a droplet (4 - 8 μL) of cell suspension on the inlet, covering the inlet hole completely.
Put the Petri dish in a vacuum for 10 min.
Release the vacuum and observe cell suspension flowing into the microchannel.
Incubate the Petri dish in an incubator to promote cell adhesion as per the specified conditions.
Add PBS to the Petri dish to submerge the PDMS device.
Peel the PDMS carefully off the petri dish with tweezers.
Wash the pattern with PBS.
Add cell culture media to the Petri dish.
Place the cell culture in the incubator.
